comments.body:
Root cause proven and fix pushed as Gerrit change 1557.

MECHANISM (confirmed by recovering the deleted event from tickets history):
ticket f103-2473-5463-4130 was compacted 2026-06-27 (commit ad3b92b88e), which DELETED
its folded sources. Recovered blob 4af47167-24f8-4814-a25f-b4f57cc30000 is the close
STATUS {current_status: in_progress -> status: closed}. Its only surviving trace was the
prior snapshot's compiled_state. The 2026-08-05 'a3-remediation: batch N' run
(4 batches, 22:13-22:41 PDT, 677 ticket dirs touched) rebuilt from the surviving files,
so the newest surviving STATUS (the open->in_progress claim) became the status.

IMPACT (reconstructed with the real reducer against baseline bba514cd33, strictly before
batch 1, then diffed against current): 1711 closed at baseline, 214 regressed off closed
(194 in_progress, 20 open) = 96 stories, 53 tasks, 45 bugs, 20 epics. Zero legitimate
reopens (no impacted ticket has a post-baseline STATUS event). Beyond status, 480 events
are missing: 219 STATUS, 181 SIGNATURE, 64 COMMENT, 8 EDIT, 4 VERIFY_COMMANDS,
4 FILE_IMPACT. 213/214 fully recoverable from history; 0241-c6c1-0a20-491b is partial.

LATENT EXPOSURE: a dry run of the FIXED fsck against the live store reports 505 tickets
whose snapshots cite source events absent from disk — still vulnerable, larger than the
already-damaged 214.

NOTE the 'pre-a3-remediation' tag points at a MID-RUN commit (2026-08-05 22:33:05, after
2 of 4 batches), so it is NOT a safe rollback point despite 34b1's rollback plan naming it.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
CI (Verified -1) on change 1559 patch set 1: my test used a `tests.`-rooted import
(`from tests.integration.test_concurrency_regression import ...`). That resolves only when the
repo root is on sys.path, which `python -m pytest` provides but the bare `pytest` console
script used by CI and `make test` does not. It tripped
tests/unit/test_tests_import_convention.py plus a collection ImportError. Fixed to the bare
module-name import (`from test_concurrency_regression import ...`); the convention test and
the four b636 tests now pass under bare pytest.

Lesson for the local verification step: run the CI selection the way CI runs it
(`pytest -m 'not integration and not external'`, bare console script), not `python -m pytest`
with a -k filter — the -k filter also hid this because the failing gate test does not match
'fsck or compact or snapshot or rebuild'.

PLAN once 1559 lands: before running the real fsck against the live store, verify the LOCAL
build actually contains the fix (this host's global rebar auto-updates from origin/main hourly,
so it can be stale):
  1. python -c 'from rebar._commands.fsck_repair import snapshot_missing_sources'  -> ImportError
     means the installed build predates the fix.
  2. rebar fsck --repair-snapshots --dry-run  -> must emit SNAPSHOT_MISSING_SOURCES and DRY-RUN
     lines; neither string exists in the pre-fix build, so their presence is a positive signal
     that the new code is live AND that the run wrote nothing.

compiled_state.description:
# fsck snapshot rebuild silently drops history that exists only in a prior SNAPSHOT

## Symptom
214 tickets that were `closed` reverted to `in_progress` (194) or `open` (20) — 96 stories,
53 tasks, 45 bugs, 20 epics. Status was not the only loss: 480 events total are missing from
disk (219 STATUS, 181 SIGNATURE, 64 COMMENT, 8 EDIT, 4 VERIFY_COMMANDS, 4 FILE_IMPACT).
Verified zero legitimate reopens: no impacted ticket has a post-baseline STATUS event.

## Root cause
Three conditions compose:

1. Compaction BEFORE `16640a705d` (2026-07-07, "retire folded events to *.retired instead of
   deleting") DELETED folded source events. Their content survived only inside the SNAPSHOT's
   `compiled_state`.
2. `compact.rebuild_snapshot_from_full_log` calls `reduce_ticket(ticket_dir,
   include_retired=True)` (compact.py:474). Rebuild mode pre-strips SNAPSHOTs and replays raw
   events from index 0 (`reducer/_replay.py:51-52`). That is correct ONLY IF the retired files
   are a complete log — false for any ticket compacted before the Jul-7 fix.
3. `rebar fsck --repair` (the A3 remediation, ticket 34b1) ran that rebuild at scale:
   4 batches on 2026-08-05 22:13-22:41 PDT (+3 on 2026-07-08), touching 677 ticket dirs.

For each affected ticket the rebuild replayed only surviving files, so the newest surviving
STATUS (typically the `open -> in_progress` claim) became the reconstructed status.

## Why the existing safety policy did not catch it
Ticket 34b1 already classifies STATUS/EDIT/FILE_IMPACT/SIGNATURE/VERIFY_COMMANDS as
HUMAN-TRIAGE ("order-sensitive ... surfaced, NOT auto-rebuilt") vs AUTO-RECOVER
(COMMENT/LINK/UNLINK/TAG_DELTA/COMMITS/BRIDGE_ALERT/REVERT). That classification gates only
WHICH ORPHAN TYPE TRIGGERS a rebuild. A rebuild is whole-ticket: once triggered by an
auto-recover orphan (or SNAPSHOT_STALE_CHANNEL), it rewrites ALL state from the incomplete
log, taking order-sensitive STATUS with it. The guard is on the trigger, not on the blast
radius.

## Secondary defect — `--dry-run` does not cover `--repair-snapshots`
`fsck.py:582` passes `no_mutate` and ignores `dry_run`, so
`rebar fsck --repair-snapshots --dry-run` MUTATES the store. Only the batched `--repair`
path honors dry-run (fsck.py:541, 567). A read-only preview of the broad legacy rebuild is
currently impossible.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `rebuild_snapshot_from_full_log` FAILS CLOSED for a ticket whose prior SNAPSHOT cites
      `source_event_uuids` with no corresponding file on disk: refuse the rebuild, surface for
      human triage, never write a lossy snapshot. Preserves the RC2b orphan-folding goal for
      tickets whose log IS complete.
- [ ] Rebuild seeds from the prior SNAPSHOT's `compiled_state` and replays only post-snapshot
      events, so state that exists only in the snapshot is never discarded while the merged-in
      orphan is still folded in.
- [ ] `--dry-run` is honored on `--repair-snapshots` (and any other mutating fsck path):
      prints the per-ticket plan, writes nothing. Regression test asserts no bytes change.
- [ ] A store-wide fsck check reports every ticket whose SNAPSHOT cites missing source events
      (the latent population), so exposure is visible before a repair runs.
- [ ] Held-out tests: a ticket compacted in the legacy delete-style whose close exists only in
      the snapshot must survive a rebuild attempt with status intact.

## Remediation of existing damage (separate change)
Restore the 480 deleted events from `origin/tickets` history (213/214 fully recoverable;
`0241-c6c1-0a20-491b` is partial — one event has no deletion record), retire the bad
Aug-5/6 snapshots, then rebuild against the now-complete log. Note the `pre-a3-remediation`
tag points at a MID-RUN commit (2026-08-05 22:33:05, after 2 of 4 batches), so it is NOT a
safe rollback point; the clean baseline is `bba514cd3318ea6b0e012e31656d3a088f419d1d`.

## FOLDED IN: fsck must RESTORE this class, not only refuse (was story 9f7f)

Fail-closed alone leaves the existing population permanently un-repairable: a dry run of the
fixed fsck reports 505 live tickets in exactly this shape, and `fsck --repair` could then
never drive them to fsck-zero. A repair tool that detects a known-fixable fault and declines
to fix it is half a fix, so the restore lands in THIS change rather than a dependent one
(splitting it created a review-ordering deadlock: 9f7f depends_on b636 fast-failed
INDETERMINATE until b636 closed).

Evidence it is auto-repairable: deleted event files stay reachable in `origin/tickets` history
at the deleting commit's parent. Over the 505 flagged tickets, 504 have deletion records
covering every cited-missing uuid, 1 partial, 0 with none. Validated end-to-end on a COPY of
the live store: restore-then-rebuild returned 214/214 already-regressed tickets to their
correct status (486 events recovered).

### Additional acceptance criteria
- [ ] `fsck_repair.restore_deleted_sources(tracker, ticket_id, ticket_dir, *, dry_run=False)`
      restores every event file ever deleted from that ticket dir, enumerated by ONE
      ticket-scoped `git log --diff-filter=D --name-only -- <tid>/` pass, each blob read at the
      deleting commit's parent and written back as a folded `.retired` source (never
      resurrected as a live event). Returns the restored filenames.
- [ ] NEWEST-deletion-wins. The walk is modelled on
      `attest.authorship.build_ticket_position_commit_map`, but that helper folds
      OLDEST-wins (correct for `--diff-filter=A`, where the oldest ADD introduced the event).
      For `--diff-filter=D` the newest removal holds the current pre-image, so first-seen
      wins over git's newest-first stream. Held-out test: a path deleted TWICE restores the
      NEWEST pre-image.
- [ ] It sweeps the ticket's FULL deletion history, NOT the newest SNAPSHOT's
      `source_event_uuids`: an earlier deleted STATUS that no surviving snapshot cites still
      breaks the chain's `current_status` precondition, so the reducer rejects both it and the
      close that follows (observed on ticket 72d5).
- [ ] `fsck_repair.rebuild_with_restore(...)` owns restore -> re-check -> rebuild and is what
      the repair path calls. The fail-closed guard still applies: if the restore cannot
      complete the log, the rebuild refuses and the ticket is surfaced for human triage.
- [ ] `SNAPSHOT_MISSING_SOURCES` joins the repairable trigger set so `fsck --repair` actually
      drives this class to zero.
- [ ] `--dry-run` reports how many events WOULD be restored and whether a rebuild would
      follow, writing nothing.
- [ ] Held-out test: a source deleted by a legacy delete-style compaction is recovered from
      history, lands as `.retired` (not live), and completes the log.
compiled_state.title: fsck snapshot rebuild silently drops history that exists only in a prior SNAPSHOT (214 tickets reverted from closed)
